sections.h2: Whom does a Brick, New Jersey owner pay?
sections.html:
The Tax Collector's office in the municipal building, 401 Chambers Bridge Road, Brick, NJ 08723. It opens on weekdays at nine and closes at four. One bill folds in municipal government, public school, county government, library, open space and fire district taxes. The township's wording is blunt: not receiving a bill does not excuse payment, and interest still runs.

Brick sits in Ocean County, so assessment disputes belong to the Ocean County Board of Taxation, which the township lists at 732-929-2008. The collector's page tells owners to send every appeal question there.

sections.h2: What are the Brick property tax installments?
sections.html:
The year is billed in four quarters, and each falls due on the first of its month. A 10 day grace period follows, and interest attaches to anything received later.

Brick Township installment calendar

Q1February 1January to March
Q2May 1April to June
Q3August 1July to September
Q4November 1October to December

Source: Brick Township Tax Collector.

A seller who is behind on any installment should get the balance, with interest, from the collector before a closing is scheduled.

sections.h2: Which payment methods work best in Brick?
sections.html:
Choose the method with the grace period in mind. Counter payments accept check, cash or credit card, and checks can be mailed to the same address. Online payment runs through Paymentus.

  • Cards online cost a 2.5 percent fee and post the next business day.
  • E-checks sit through a 10 business day hold under bank network rules, so they can land after the grace period and draw interest.
  • Automatic withdrawal needs a short form and a voided check, adds no cost, and pulls funds inside the grace period. Cancel in writing before a due date.
  • Never mail card numbers, and expect no Paymentus option for tax sale items or lien redemptions.

To redeem a lien, write at least 72 hours ahead with the block, lot and lien number and the date payment will reach the office. Certified funds, cash or a money order are the only forms accepted.

sections.h2: What are Brick's homes and residents like?
sections.html:
Five year survey results for 2020 to 2024 give $410,600 as the middle value for an owned home and $106,130 as the typical household income. Homeowners make up 82.2 percent of households. The township's estimated 2025 population is 77,402, a 5.1 percent rise on the 2020 base of 73,654.

  • 30,289 households of about 2.47 people each.
  • 21.4 percent of residents at least 65.
  • Rent of $1,756 a month.
  • Owner costs of $2,310 with a mortgage and $949 without.
  • A 28.2 minute average trip to work.

Brick covers 32.22 square miles, a fifth of it water. The mainland is joined by ocean beach sections on the Barnegat Peninsula that do not touch it. The township was incorporated February 15, 1850 and named for Joseph W. Brick, who owned the Bergen Iron Works on the Metedeconk River. When the Garden State Parkway came through in 1954, a long housing boom produced neighborhoods such as Lake Riviera, Laurelton and Baywood. Brick Township High School opened in 1958, and in 2006 the thirteenth annual Morgan Quitno survey of 371 cities named the township America's safest city.

sections.h2: What is an added assessment in Brick?
sections.html:
It is the extra tax on new construction. When work is finished, the township assesses the improvement and mails an Added Assessment Bill in October, payable November 1 with the fourth quarter, then February 1 and May 1 of the following year. It is combined with the regular bill that arrived in June or July, and the next June bill merges everything.

The township's building office adds that unpermitted work tends to surface at sale. A buyer's inspector asks for proof that additions were approved, and state law lets officials levy up to $2,000 plus $2,000 for each week a violation continues. Sales have collapsed or dropped in price when such work was found. Pull your permits and final approvals for any finished basement, deck or addition before you list.

sections.h2: What does a Brick seller need besides tax payoffs?
sections.html:
No certificate of occupancy is demanded when a Brick house is resold. The seller must still get the Bureau of Fire Safety's compliance certificate for smoke detectors, carbon monoxide detectors and a fire extinguisher, and the bureau's number is 732-458-4100. An oil tank in use and not leaking can stay put, and removal becomes a point for the buyer and seller to negotiate.

  • Rentals need a certificate for each new tenant, and landlords register through the Township Clerk for $100.
  • Weeds and grass may not top 10 inches.
  • Unregistered vehicles belong in a garage, not on the lot.
  • Owners clear the sidewalk and the strip to the curb, snow included.

The building office points owners to FEMA's lookup for flood zones but notes that only a licensed surveyor can settle one. Its design table lists a 115 mph wind load and a 30 inch frost depth. Rain and melted snow add up to about 46 inches a year, and February is the peak month for nor'easter snow.

sections.h2: Which schools and roads does Brick have?
sections.html:
Brick Public Schools operate 12 schools from preschool through grade 12 and enrolled 8,414 students in 2020 to 2021. Brick Memorial and Brick Township are the high schools, and Lake Riviera and Veterans Memorial are the middle schools. Private choices include St. Dominic Elementary and St. Paul's Christian School.

The Garden State Parkway cuts through the west side with exits 89, 90 and 91, and routes 35, 70 and 88 cross town. As of 2010 the township kept up about 256 of its 319 road miles. Herbertsville and Parkway Pines lie by Exit 91 at the Monmouth County line, apart from the rest of Brick.

Commuters have NJ Transit bus routes to Midtown Manhattan (route 137), Newark (67) and Camden (317), and an Academy Bus line runs from the Parkway to Lower Manhattan. The Brick Township Park and Ride at Exit 91 offers an express run to New York City at rush hour. Ocean Ride routes 3, 3A and 4 serve local trips.

The township maintains nearly a dozen community parks, the Drum Point Sports Complex, three oceanfront beaches and Windward Beach Park on the Metedeconk River. Brick Township Reservoir, shared with Wall Township, covers 80 acres, has a 1.7 mile trail and allows fishing. The Ocean Ice Palace, built in 1960, hosts the Brick Hockey Club, and the Havens Homestead Museum in Laurelton and Burrsville preserves the story of the family that first settled there.

faqs.q: Where is a Brick property tax payment made?
faqs.a: At the Tax Collector, 401 Chambers Bridge Road, Brick, NJ 08723, in person between nine and four on weekdays, by mail, or online through Paymentus, which charges 2.5 percent on cards. Counter payments can be made with a check, cash or a credit card, and checks may also be mailed to that address.

faqs.q: Which board decides a Brick assessment appeal?
faqs.a: The Ocean County Board of Taxation, listed by the township at 732-929-2008. State rules put the petition date at April 1, or May 1 after a municipal revaluation or reassessment.

faqs.q: Is there any grace after a Brick due date?
faqs.a: Yes, 10 days. Interest applies after that, and e-checks may miss the window because of a 10 business day processing hold. Direct withdrawals from a bank account draw during the grace period.

faqs.q: Must a Brick seller obtain a certificate of occupancy?
faqs.a: No, the township does not ask for one on resale. A fire safety certificate is still needed, and the Bureau of Fire Safety at 732-458-4100 issues it.

faqs.q: What does Brick mean by an Added Assessment Bill?
faqs.a: It is the bill for finished new construction, mailed in October. It comes due November 1, then February 1 and May 1 the next year, and the following June bill merges it with the regular tax.
